about: The shape every Quillstack package takes, in whatever language it is written. Rules marked universal hold everywhere; the rest name the ecosystem they belong to.

rendering.note: An inline element at the end of a line with a link starting the next renders with the space between them missing: `**with**` and `[a link]` come out as `witha link`.

badges.note: A badge that 404s is worse than no badge. Each is fetched, not eyeballed. The list is what every ecosystem carries. A service which exists for one language only is named in that language's section instead: StyleCI checks PHP style and has nothing to say about Python, so it is not here.

repository.note: The address carries the language. `/packages/<name>` was PHP's before there was a second language and is kept, because it is in the metadata of released packages and a redirect is a promise you keep for ever; PHP's checker fills `{language}` with nothing and Python's with `python`.

ci.note: A tag is a pointer its owner can move. The comment is what Dependabot reads, so it has to be true.

documentation.note: The page is built from the README. There is no second copy to keep in step.

quality.note: A project imported before its first analysis is created with `master` as the main branch, and without a new code period the quality gate is never computed. Both have been missed five times by hand.

releasing.note: Tagging is not publishing: a registry hears about a tag through a webhook, and a webhook can fail. One did here and answered 500, so a release looked done — green CI, tag on GitHub — and nobody could install it. It went unnoticed long enough for the next release to be missing too.

python.note: Filled in as the Python side is built. The universal rules above already apply to it. No style badge yet: ruff is the formatter and linter, and it runs in CI rather than as a service with a shield.

classifiers.note: A distribution with no classifiers renders a `python` badge reading `missing`, because shields.io reads the classifiers rather than `requires-python`. One version classifier per supported version.
